subject: How can I construct single-indicator latent variable model?

messages.author: 4a0d6ff9ce3b1d6b
messages.subject: How can I construct single-indicator latent variable model?
parts:
Hello community members,

● What I actually want to do
- I'm trying to analyze panel data with lavaan package (cross-lagged effect model).
- If I could I wanted to run following code

model <- '
# Observed variables A,B,C,D are ordinal variables
f1 =~ 1*A1 + B1;  
f2 =~ 1*A2 + B2;
f3 =~ 1*C1 + D1;
f4 =~ 1*C2 + D2;

f3 ~ f1 + f2;
f4 ~ f1 + f2
'
result <- sem(model, data, ordered = c("A", "B", "C", "D"))

● Problem
- But I actually don't have D1 (in 3rd line in the former model).

● My code
- So I changed my model to one containing single-indicator latent variable.
- As follows, I fix the coefficient of the C1 at one and error variance of it 

f1 =~ 1*A1 + B1;  
f2 =~ 1*A2 + B2;
f3 =~ 1*C1;
f4 =~ 1*C2 + D2;

#Raw Cronbach's alpha is 0.783 and var is 0.957
C1 ~~ (1-0.783)*0.957*C1

f3 ~ f1 + f2;
f4 ~ f1 + f2
'
result <- sem(model, data, ordered = c("A", "B", "C", "D"))

But I still have these warning messages.

lavaan WARNING:
    Could not compute standard errors! The information matrix could
    not be inverted. This may be a symptom that the model is not
    identified.
lavaan WARNING: could not invert information matrix needed for robust test statistic

- How can I solve this problem and identify the models?

I thank you in advance.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: How can I construct single-indicator latent variable model?
parts: I fix the coefficient of the C1 at one and error variance of it

C1 is ordinal, so its (error) variance is not modeled.  The variance of its latent response (assumed normal) is assumed 1 by default (parameterization = "delta"), and its error variance is simply 1 minus the variance explained by the common factor.  Because f3 is not a common factor (only a single indicator), you don't have enough information to identify its variance.  So specifying a single ordinal indicator would be accomplished by using parameterization = "theta" (so the error variances are model parameters instead of the scales of the latent item responses), in which case all indicators are identified by fixing their error variances to 1.  Thus, you would fix the single-indicator's error variance to zero and its factor variance to one, if you assumed the single indicator were without measurement error.

To account for unreliability of the indicator, you would fix the error variance to 1 - alpha instead of zero, and fix the factor variance to alpha instead of 1.

#Raw Cronbach's alpha is 0.783 and var is 0.957
C1 ~~ (1-0.783)*0.957*C1

Actually do the math, so you can put the fixed values in the syntax.

C1 ~~ 0.217*C1
f3 ~~ 0.783*f3
